conclusion: No data or estimand discrepancy. Small endpoint differences are finite-bootstrap Monte Carlo variation from different seeds AND equivalent but different random sampling implementations. Existing sealed reports remain unchanged.

analysis_bootstrap.sampling: uniform source-index sampling with replacement via numpy default_rng.choice, then sum selected source means
analysis_bootstrap.quantile: numpy.quantile [.025,.975], default linear interpolation; multiply paired gain samples by100 before quantile

executor_bootstrap.sampling: multinomial source multiplicity weights via numpy default_rng.multinomial, then weighted sum of source means
executor_bootstrap.quantile: numpy.quantile [.025,.975], default linear interpolation; multiply quantiles by100 afterwards

shared_estimand.unit: whole episode source, all four suffixes/all methods remain paired
shared_estimand.strata: five tasks,60sources each in total cohort
shared_estimand.source_weights: equal per-source, preserve observed task counts

interpretation: Multinomial counts and direct sampling with replacement induce the same empirical bootstrap distribution. They consume RNG streams differently; matching seed alone would not make finite draws identical.
Multiplication by100 before versus after a linear percentile is mathematically equivalent; floating-point roundoff is negligible compared with observed0.0833pp endpoint differences.
One total-cohort paired-success count is100/1200=0.083333pp, matching the observed one-grid-step endpoint shifts.
All three A intervals cross0 in both reports; methodological conclusion and formal training release are unchanged.
